name: barrow

attributes.attribute: a pre-Celtic grave built of a line of stones ending in a mound
sometimes holds more than one burial
carries the largest group of barrows in England

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
A barrow is a pre-Celtic grave. Builders set stones in a line that ends in a burial mound. Some barrows hold more than one body.

The Wiltshire Downs carry the largest group of barrows in England. Stonehenge rises above those downs. Barrows also appear throughout Ireland. Local people revere the graves near their homes. They tell tales of hauntings at the mounds. Black Dogs of the fairy race and wandering ghosts frequent these sites. See the entry for the Fairy Mound.

okr.objective: Describe the barrow as a pre-Celtic burial site and the folklore attached to it.
key_results: A barrow is a grave of pre-Celtic origin built from stones.
The Wiltshire Downs hold the largest group of barrows in England.
Barrows appear across Ireland and are linked to hauntings.
